name: Seven Questions Before You Sign
why_it_works: People feel outmatched in paperwork-heavy decisions. A checklist of questions hands them leverage, and it is built to be saved and screenshotted right before a meeting. The brand that gives you the questions is the one you trust to answer them.

hook.pattern: Give the viewer a script to use on any provider before committing.
examples: Seven questions to ask before you sign any {{document}}.
If they can't answer number four, don't sign.

variables.name: meeting_type
variables.description: The appointment the viewer is heading into

variables.name: question_1
variables.example: What is my total cost over the first five years?

variables.name: question_3
variables.example: What happens if I pay early?

variables.name: question_4
variables.example: Who do I call if something goes wrong after closing?

variables.name: question_5
variables.example: What would make this rate change before closing?

variables.name: question_6
variables.example: What do you earn on this, and how?

variables.name: question_7
variables.example: What would you do in my position, and why?

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, from compliance/packs.json

slides.headline: 7 questions before you sign any {{document}}
slides.visual_prompt: Clean title card: a pen hovering over a signature line, shallow depth of field, {{brand}} colors, 4:5

slides.headline: 1. Ask the long-term cost
slides.visual_prompt: Large numeral 1 over a soft-focus calculator and paperwork, neutral light

slides.headline: 2. Ask what bends
slides.visual_prompt: Large numeral 2 over a fee sheet with one line circled in pen

slides.headline: 3. Ask about the exit
slides.visual_prompt: Large numeral 3 over an open door in a bright office hallway

slides.headline: 4. The one they dodge
slides.body: {{question_4}} If the answer is vague, pause.
slides.visual_prompt: Large numeral 4 in red over an empty office chair, slightly cooler light

slides.headline: 5. Ask what can change
slides.visual_prompt: Large numeral 5 over a calendar with a date circled

slides.headline: 6. Ask how they get paid
slides.visual_prompt: Large numeral 6 over two coffee cups on a meeting table

slides.headline: 7. Ask what they'd do
slides.visual_prompt: Large numeral 7 over a person listening across a desk, warm light

slides.headline: Bring these to {{brand}}
slides.body: We'll answer all seven in writing: {{offer}}. {{disclosure}}
slides.visual_prompt: {{brand}} logo card with the offer in large type and a phone-friendly booking line

craft.technique: Save-bait checklist with a planted weak point
craft.notes: One question is flagged as the dodge (slide 4, in red). That single tension point turns a dry list into a test the viewer wants to run. The final slide has the brand volunteer to be tested, which is the trust move.

do_not: Include questions {{brand}} cannot answer cleanly in writing
Turn questions into disguised sales claims
Put more than one question per slide
compliance: Mortgage: no rate or approval promises; any rate shown needs APR and required disclosures; include NMLS ID and Equal Housing Opportunity
Insurance: no coverage or savings guarantees; include license number where your state requires
Law firms: questions are general information, not legal advice; add an attorney-advertising label if your state requires
Financial advisor: no return promises; follow FINRA/SEC advertising rules and disclose how you are compensated if asked in slide 6
Real estate: include brokerage name and license info per state rules
